next.name: Threat Group-3390
next.headline: Threat Group-3390: a long-running espionage group known as Emissary Panda, APT27 and LuckyMouse
next.in_short: Threat Group-3390 goes by many names. Dell SecureWorks, Symantec and Germany's BfV describe it as a China-based espionage group. Reports show watering holes, unpatched servers and backdoors such as PlugX and HyperBro.

sentences.t: The MITRE-sourced catalogue record lists these names for the group: Threat Group-3390, TG-3390, Earth Smilodon, Emissary Panda, BRONZE UNION, APT27, Iron Tiger, LuckyMouse and Linen Typhoon.
Dell SecureWorks researchers designated the group Threat Group 3390 and nicknamed it Emissary Panda. The article reporting their work describes the group as believed to be based in China.
Symantec's Threat Hunter Team calls the group Budworm, also known as LuckyMouse, Emissary Panda and APT27. It reports that the group is believed to have been active since at least 2013.
Germany's Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) describes APT27, also known as Emissary Panda, as a Chinese cyberespionage group.
Microsoft Threat Intelligence says Linen Typhoon has focused on stealing intellectual property since 2012.

SecureWorks said most of the group's early targets were in the automotive, electronic, aerospace, energy and pharmaceutical industries. It said at least 50 organizations in the US and the United Kingdom had data stolen.

The same research listed defense contractors, universities, law firms and political organizations among the targets. A cultural site for the Uyghur ethnic group was also used, apparently to target members of that minority for surveillance.

Symantec describes Budworm as often focusing on government, technology and defense organizations. It reported attacks in August 2023 on a Middle Eastern telecommunications organization and an Asian government.
The BfV says APT27 repeatedly attacked German companies, with attacks going back to at least March 2021.
A malware catalogue entry says the HyperBro remote access trojan has been observed targeting primarily the gambling industry, though it has been seen elsewhere too.

In 2015, SecureWorks described watering hole attacks launched from over 100 compromised legitimate websites. No zero-day flaws were used. The group relied on old ones, including CVE-2011-3544 and CVE-2010-0738, and used the PlugX remote access tool.
The BfV says the later German attacks hit unpatched, internet-exposed servers. It names flaws in Microsoft Exchange and Zoho ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus, and says the final payload was HyperBro.

Symantec says Budworm ran its SysUpdate backdoor through DLL sideloading. It also used living-off-the-land and publicly available tools such as AdFind, SecretsDump and PasswordDumper to map networks and dump credentials.
One entry describes HyperBro as typically having three or more components. These include a genuine loader and an encrypted, compressed payload.
A detection test-case page cites Threat Group 3390 (Bronze Union) as an example of disabling HTTP logging on a Windows IIS web server.

A report on the Redosdru downloader says it is commonly associated with APT27/Iron Tiger. The catalogue record also lists tools such as PlugX, China Chopper, Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, HyperBro and SysUpdate.
Recorded Future lists LuckyMouse (TG-3390, Emissary Panda, Bronze Union) among actors that have historically used the Scanbox reconnaissance framework.
SecureWorks unveiled its report on the group at the Black Hat conference. The article about it was published on 5 August 2015.
The BfV warned about APT27 activity against German companies. It said it cannot rule out that the actors also try to reach customers or service providers, which would be a supply chain attack.
Symantec said the August 2023 attacks may have been stopped early. The only malicious activity it saw on infected machines was credential harvesting.

Microsoft says Linen Typhoon and Violet Typhoon, two Chinese nation-state actors, exploited on-premises SharePoint vulnerabilities. Microsoft's analysis suggests attempts began as early as 7 July 2025.
A report on attacks on Southeast Asian organizations lists Budworm among groups whose tools were seen. It says specific attribution is not possible because these groups often share tools.
Kaspersky's GReAT team says its EastWind campaign used a new PlugY implant. The report says PlugY shares code with the DRBControl backdoor, which several companies attribute to APT27.
Patch internet-facing servers promptly. Several of the reports above describe attacks that began with unpatched systems.
Watch web server logging settings, since attackers may switch logging off to leave less evidence.
